annotations.keyFindings: Pharmacist follow-up raised pill-count adherence to 91 against 79 percent at 12 weeks; admissions 9 against 15 percent, compatible with chance; relative dose intensity 0.87 against 0.92.
annotations.limitations: 212 patients; not powered for admissions; pill count only.

annotations.keyFindings: A clinic for 400 patients cost about 118,000 a year; averted admissions were valued at 64,000 to 141,000 a year, presented as a budget range.
annotations.limitations: Before-after admission rates unadjusted; patient costs excluded.

annotations.keyFindings: Refill data overestimated adherence against electronic caps by 8 to 12 points; self-report was highest at 97 percent.
Telephone toxicity checks were followed by severe toxicity falling from 21 to 13 percent, with lower relative dose intensity (0.86 against 0.91).
Patients valued a named pharmacist to call; some found repeated calls intrusive; people living alone or with limited English struggled most but were under-represented.
Across 31 studies, adherence effects were inconsistent and measured six ways; 7 reported admissions and 4 reported costs; few included patients over 75.
Eighteen percent were admitted within 90 days, half for toxicity; risk was higher over 75, living alone and more than 100 kilometres away.
Pharmacist time per patient over 12 weeks was a median of 2.6 hours (1.4 to 4.1 between centres).
annotations.limitations: Eight weeks of timing at four centres.

claims.text: In a trial of 212 adults, adherence by pill count at 12 weeks was 91 percent with pharmacist follow-up against 79 percent with usual care.
claims.passage: At 12 weeks, adherence by pill count was 91 percent with pharmacist follow-up and 79 percent with usual care.
claims.interpretation: Adherence strand: one trial, one measure.

claims.text: Pharmacy refill data overestimated adherence compared with electronic caps by 8 to 12 percentage points.

claims.text: Unplanned admission risk after starting oral anticancer agents was higher in patients over 75, living alone or far from the centre.
claims.passage: Risk was higher in patients over 75, patients living alone and those living more than 100 kilometres from the centre.
claims.interpretation: The committee summary must say these groups are thinly covered by intervention studies.

synthesis: Eight retrieved records of the 19 hits the search reported, appraised at abstract level; 11 hits were not ingested and are unappraised. Adherence: one trial found higher pill-count adherence with pharmacist follow-up, but measures disagree by up to 12 points and a review found inconsistent effects. Harms: severe toxicity fell after pharmacist toxicity checks in a historical comparison, with lower dose intensity as a balancing concern; admissions did not differ clearly in the trial. Time and money: about 2.6 pharmacist hours per patient over 12 weeks; one centre's budget range for averted admissions overlapped the clinic's cost. Patients valued a named pharmacist, and the groups at highest risk were least studied.
gradeRationale: One small trial, historical comparisons, one budget analysis and a review of inconsistent studies; low certainty for adherence and harms, very low for costs, and incomplete because 11 hits were not ingested.
summary: Eight of 19 hits appraised; seven claims in separate strands; certainty low.
